subject: Unable to see graphs when running ggvis-demo code using "source()" in a directory

messages.author: 5e0a072a41164542
messages.subject: Unable to see graphs when running ggvis-demo code using "source()" in a directory
parts:
I created a folder and included all the 'rstudio/ggvis/demo' code in a directory on my computer.

When I start R in that directory (double click on .Rdata) and do “source(‘bar.r’)” (or any other r code in that directory), no graph comes out.

I can tell the code runs, because it gives text version output in R console window, but I can not see graphics which are supposed to be created. I tried both Rgui and Rstudio, but couldn’t get either to work.

Anybody has an idea?

messages.subject: Re: Unable to see graphs when running ggvis-demo code using "source()" in a directory
parts:
Thank you Hadley! It's helpful.

I added "%>% print()" after the statement of ggvis graphs, and it works.

For example, the first graphic in "bar.r", save the code as following and "source('bar.r')"

# Bar graph with continuous x, and y value supplied in the data

pressure %>% ggvis(x = ~temperature, y = ~pressure) %>%

  layer_bars() %>% print()

On Thursday, June 26, 2014 12:44:21 PM UTC-5, Hadley Wickham wrote:
You'll need to explicit print the plots to see them.
Hadley
